about.privacy.title: Local-first & privacy boundaries
about.privacy.text:
• Arenyxa core tasks, databases, search indexes, and settings are stored locally by default and do not require an official Arenyxa cloud account.
• Core collection, parsing, search, export, and network analysis use local deterministic workflows.
• Target websites and user-enabled server, marketplace, or network-analysis features access the network as required by their purpose; local-first does not mean “never networked.”
• Sensitive values such as Cookie, Authorization, and Token are redacted by default at logging, diagnostics, and plugin boundaries.

about.capabilities.title: Core capabilities
about.capabilities.text: Capture & Replay · HTTP / Browser / Packet · Search & Data · Dataset Revision · Visualization\nWorkflow & Automation · Headless Server / RBAC · Plugins & Sandbox · Terminal / Packet Console\nRepair Center · Release Provenance · Liquid Glass & Professional Motion · 10 Languages / RTL
about.detail.development: Source mode permits normal modification; integrity checks do not treat ordinary development changes as tampering requiring forced recovery.
about.detail.verified_official: The release attestation was verified against the built-in official trust root. Deep verification can additionally check all signed files and loadable code.
about.detail.verified_community: The release signature is valid, but the identity belongs to a community or third-party distribution and does not represent official Arenyxa endorsement.
about.detail.modified: Installed content differs from the signed release manifest. The software remains usable, but it can no longer claim to be an unmodified verified distribution.
about.detail.unverified: This distribution has no verifiable release attestation. That does not imply malware, but official provenance cannot be confirmed.
about.detail.invalid: The release attestation, signature chain, or release manifest is invalid. For installed builds, run deep verification and use Repair Center according to the result.
about.provenance.scope_quick: Quick status verifies release attestation only; file-by-file installation verification is performed only by “Deep-verify installation.”
about.provenance.scope_deep: The current identity state includes the result of this deep installation-integrity verification.
about.verify.running: Checking release attestation, signed manifest, installed files, additional loadable code, recovery payloads, and SQLite integrity…
about.verify.unrecognized: Deep verification returned an unrecognized result.
about.verify.no_provenance: Deep verification did not return a release-integrity result.
about.verify.offline: Deep verification reads only local installation content and database integrity information; no network connection is required.
developer.terms.risk_text:
Developer Mode enables advanced diagnostics, controlled external commands, full-function validation, and high-load stability testing.

When enabled, tests may significantly increase CPU, memory, disk, and local-loopback load and may trigger optional components, drivers, or security software. Full-function validation uses isolated temporary directories and 127.0.0.1 loopback services by default and does not proactively access public Internet targets; high-load tests also do not intentionally write to formal project data.

Use these capabilities only on devices and data environments you own or are authorized to test. Save active work before testing and stop immediately if abnormal behavior is observed.
developer.terms.waiver_text:
Developer testing is intended to reveal defects, performance boundaries, and stability issues; it is not a guarantee of fault-free operation on specific hardware, drivers, third-party components, or extreme load conditions.

High-load tests use bounded stress models: concurrency increases progressively and stops when errors, resource anomalies, or built-in safety limits are detected. The tests are not designed to intentionally exhaust system memory, fill the disk, or make the operating system unresponsive.

Continuing indicates that you understand these risks and will decide whether the current device is appropriate for developer testing.
